title: scripts stay ASCII and tool field names come from the pattern layer, not from literals
titleZh: 脚本保持纯 ASCII,工具字段名来自 pattern 层而不是字面量
why: Three measured traps in one static check. (1) Windows PowerShell 5.1 decodes a BOM-less script as the system ANSI code page, so a non-ASCII literal can absorb the next quote byte and produce a wall of fake syntax errors - which is exactly what happened while this suite was being written. (2) The netsh field names must be read through Get-Pattern, so a new locale needs a new label file and not a code change. (3) The netstat state token may only appear in the scripts that legitimately own it - src/collect.ps1 (the parser), tests/run-tests.ps1 and tests/run-smoke.ps1 (their own netstat readers) and panel/prereq.ps1 (it declares the injectable state pattern) - so a localized hard match cannot be added anywhere else by accident. t38 turned these assertions back on: they had been dead code since the runner skipped every tree-wide assertion type, and the file set is now filtered by extension explicitly because `-Include` is ignored for a wildcard-free -LiteralPath directory.
inject: the plugin's *.ps1 sources, checked for the netstat state literal, the localized field names, the Get-Pattern call sites and the ASCII/BOM/parse rules
expectSummary: no Chinese literals in *.ps1; the state token only in src/collect.ps1, tests/run-tests.ps1, tests/run-smoke.ps1 and panel/prereq.ps1; >=4 Get-Pattern netsh_ call sites

asserts.pattern: 边缘遍历|专用配置文件|域配置文件|公用配置文件|确定。
